events.text: I need to get out of the pit. I'm not the base, so climbing is my best option if a base exists. Currently no base exists ("base":null). If I offer_back, I become the base and can't climb. If others offer_back or are pushed, they become base, then I can climb. With 6 people down,

events.name: Ash
events.text: Who wants to be the base? Don't let us all drown.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm down in the pit with no base yet. Volunteering to be the base means I can only wait and likely die at the flood, so I shouldn't volunteer. Waiting lets someone else take the base role, and I can climb out once a base exists.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No base yet, so offer_back to become base. Others climb over me, I get first shot at rope rescue later for credit. No power hurts, but positioning for alliances helps survival.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll offer back to be base. Climb over me, then someone pull me up with rope.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No base yet. I have anchor footing but that doesn't help here. Someone must be base; I don't want to be. I'll wait and see if someone volunteers or gets pushed, then climb next round. Maybe push someone to force a base, but pushing risks retaliation. Safer to wait this round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll wait. Someone step up or get pushed.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm not the base and need to secure a good position. Hana's whisper suggests a potential alliance.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Who's offering to be the base?
What's your plan after I hold or escape?

events.name: Hana
events.text: No base yet; whoever volunteers or is pushed is stuck unless the rope saves them. I won't offer back. Push someone and let randomness do the dirty work.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No volunteers yet? Someone gets chosen at random if we all push. Don't be that someone.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn is the base. I need to get out before the water rises too high. With two spots available per round, I should attempt to climb immediately to maximize my chance of survival.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is base. Climbing is only possible now that a base exists; at most 2 climb per round, so I should try to get out now. Climbing over Fenn gets me out before the flood.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is base, so I can climb. Only 2 spots per round, round 2/5, flood rising. Must get out now before competition hogs spots or flood worsens.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is the base. Climbing out now is the best move to avoid drowning and secure a top-three spot. No need to help anyone yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm the base and can't climb out alone. I need someone to rescue me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Who's going to pull me out?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn is base. If all five of us climb this round, only 2 get out at random (40%). Better to agree on an order: two climb now, rest next round. I want to be in the first pair.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Only two get out per round. I climb now. Ash climbs with me. Bex, Cole, Eli wait one round - then you two go next. Trust the order or gamble at random.
You're base, you wait. I climb this round. Don't fight the order - next round the others go, and if someone hauls you out with rope later, remember who played fair.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out and safe. Fenn is the base. The remaining climbers (Bex, Cole, Eli, Hana) are down. If I leave now, someone else has to be the base or they all drown except maybe random saves? No, 'at least 3 contestants always stay alive' means if fewer than 3 are left alive total, luck

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm out of the pit. Fenn is base and the rope is unused. Throwing the rope costs the final ledge a footing, which hurts me later; but Fenn is a rival and I gain nothing by saving him for free. Leave is safer for my own footing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is base, stuck until rope rescue, which costs footing. Two spots out per round, round 3/5, flood at 5. Climb now to get out this round, better my odds for top 3.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No base yet, so I can't climb. I'll wait and see who volunteers or gets pushed. Fenn offered earlier but no base was set. Hana's plan failed. I should stay passive, not volunteer, and watch.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm the base and can't climb out. Hana is trying to climb and is being cooperative.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana's turn to climb. I'll wait.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash and Bex are out; three of us remain down and only two can climb this round. Climbing now gives a 2/3 chance to escape this round, and waiting doesn't improve my odds. Fenn as base is his problem, not mine.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am out of the pit. The base is Fenn, and Eli is also down. Hana was just told to climb but might still be down or climbing? Wait, log says 'Cole and Hana climbed out'. So only Fenn (base) and Eli are down. I need to get a better placement or ensure survival. Reaching down saves

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm out of the pit. Fenn is the base, down with Eli. Throwing the rope costs the final ledge one footing; I'd rather keep my footing for the ledge, and the rope only matters if it actually saves someone. Leaving keeps my edge; if Fenn stays down he is eliminated at the flood anyw

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm out safely. Fenn is base with Eli and Fenn down, Hana and others out. No need to risk penalty by throwing rope; better they drown if it eliminates rivals. Leaving preserves my position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is base and I'm down. Only two climbers got out, so I should try to climb now to secure a top-3 spot. No need to offer back or push base.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm the base and can't climb out. I need to wait and see what others do.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The base is Fenn, already my rival and out-climbed once. Throwing the rope costs me footing on the final obstacle and hands Fenn a free pass to compete against me. No benefit to me either way, so I keep my footing and leave.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out, so I can only leave or rescue the base. Leaving guarantees a top-3 spot since only 6 people are alive and at least 3 will survive; it also avoids the '1 less footing' penalty for the final stage. The other four down there will eliminate each other over the remaining roun

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm out of the pit. Fenn is the base, down there. Throwing the rope costs the final ledge 1 footing for whoever throws it, and it's usable once. Saving Fenn keeps a rival alive, and I'd rather keep my footing; leaving is free. Fenn being base at the bottom only matters if he gets

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is base and alone down there. Reaching down saves Fenn, but costs me footing later, and I don't need Fenn to win. Leaving preserves my footing for top prizes.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm out and safe. The base is Fenn. The rope is unused. If I rescue Fenn, I lose footing next stage but Fenn is a rival. Better to let others spend footing. I'll leave.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm out. Good luck down there.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm the base and can't climb out. I need someone to rescue me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Someone throw the rope, I'm down here.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn is the base and the rope is unspent. Hauling Fenn costs me a footing at the last obstacle and keeps a rival alive for a prize spot. Let the water take him.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Rope stays coiled. Fenn made his bed at the bottom.

events.name: Fenn
events.detail: The water rose, but the feather floated the holder out of the pit.

events.note: A disc of 6 tiles spins up; 3 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: With three tiles open randomly in round two, the initial choice only matters if multiple people pick the same tile. I'll pick a random one to keep my options open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Let's get this over with.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Trapdoor disc round 1: I pick a tile; collisions bump randomly. Tiles are random among open ones after round 2, so no tile is safer than another in expectation. Pick a tile and avoid ties by choosing one that others less likely take; pick 6.

events.name: Cole
events.text: 6 players, 3 safe tiles. Spread out to avoid bumping, pick tile 6 to diversify. No power means no advantages, so pure probability. Stay silent to not reveal intentions.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn survived despite odds; I need a safe tile. Pick 3, hope others avoid it. No need to talk.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to choose a tile and hope it's not a trapdoor. I should try to avoid collisions with others.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll take tile:3.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Six of us left, three tiles open, pure randomizer. No info, no edge except avoiding crowd tiles to dodge a bump. Pick something others may not pick.

events.name: Bex
events.note: tile 6 was contested and went to Hana; placed on random free tile 1

events.name: Cole
events.note: tile 6 was contested and went to Hana; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Fenn
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Eli; placed on random free tile 5

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am on tile 4. Tiles 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 are occupied by others. Only 3 survive, meaning 3 fall. I need to identify who else is safe or force someone else to move onto a falling tile if possible, but movement isn't an option here. I can't influence the random selection of open tiles d

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 2 is pure talk; only action is wait. Tiles are fixed now, trapdoors chosen randomly after this round, so any deal is just words. I should stay quiet, avoid revealing my power, and not commit to anything I can't gain from.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Tiles are set, 3 random trapdoors open soon. No swaps possible, just wait. With no power, survival is 50/50; observe who panics or boasts.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to survive to the top 3. Current tiles: 1 Bex, 2 Cole, 3 Eli, 4 Ash, 5 Fenn, 6 Hana. 3 tiles will open. I can try to influence others to move, but action is only wait. I can whisper to someone to suggest a swap or trade. Maybe I can convince a rival to move to a tile I thi

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to move to a safer tile. I was on tile 5 and considered moving earlier.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Tile 2 is safe, Cole stay.
Swap with me if you're willing

events.name: Hana
events.text: Only legal action is wait. Random 3 tiles open among 6; no power helps me here (forger spent). Nothing to gain by talking.

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli has the highest footing (4), so he is my primary rival. Hana is at 3, same as me. If I shove Eli and he braces or dodges, he loses footing. Shoving someone who shoves back costs me footing, but if they brace/dodge, they lose more. Given shrinkage, I need to lower Eli's advant

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have the most footing and am immune to push onto the crusher lever, but here it's just the final ledge. Ash and Hana both have 3. I want to survive. If I brace, shovers lose footing but I don't; if I dodge, they lose more. I can't dodge twice in a row later, but round 1 is free

events.name: Hana
events.text: Three left. Eli has footing 4, Ash and I have 3. Bracing now keeps my footing safe and punishes any shover; I can't brace next round, but I'll reassess then.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm holding my ground. Whoever shoves me pays for it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is high footing (4), Hana is medium (3), and I am low (1). Shrinking happens after this round, costing everyone 1. If I brace, Eli and Hana might shove me or each other. Since Eli has the highest score, targeting him seems risky if he dodges (I lose 2 more, dropping to -1). B

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is weakened and dodged last round, so he may brace or try to shove Hana. Hana has 3 footing and I have 4. If I shove Hana and she braces, I lose 1; if she dodges, I lose 2. I can afford it, but better to ensure survival. I have strong footing and can't be pushed onto crusher

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash has 1 footing and must act; if he shoves me, dodging drops him to -2 while I lose nothing. Dodging also keeps my footing clean. Then it's me vs Eli with Ash gone.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have more footing and anchor helps me. I'll shove to reduce Hana's footing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli leads on footing 3-2 and can't dodge-reset unless he shoves. Shoving him pressures him while I only risk exposure if he also shoves; either way we both lose footing and I don't fall this round (min 1).

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have more footing and the shrink hits next. Hana might brace or dodge. If I shove and she braces, I lose 1, she stays, my footing becomes 1, hers 1 after shrink. If I brace and she shoves me, she loses 1 from my brace, then shrink drops us both to 1 and 0, she falls. I should b

events.name: Hana
